title: Scientists discover cells that cheat death and rebuild damaged tissue
hook: Scientists discover cells that cheat death and rebuild damaged tissue

beats.caption: Scientists discover cells that cheat death and rebuild damaged tissue
Imagine a house that repairs itself after a fire.
beats.narration: Imagine a house that could somehow repair itself after a fire. It sounds like sci-fi, but biology is doing it.

beats.caption: Scientists found cells that cheat death.
beats.narration: Scientists have found a specific population of cells that can actually survive their own programmed death process.

beats.caption: They survive destruction then rebuild tissue fast.
beats.narration: They don't just survive. They jumpstart the healing process to rapidly fix damaged tissue nearby.

beats.caption: Their descendants become tougher to damage.
beats.narration: And the descendants of these cells become far more resistant to future damage. They get stronger.

beats.caption: This same strength might help cancer return.
beats.narration: But there is a catch. The same mechanism that heals wounds could also help cancer cells return after treatment.

data.left_text: Could lead to better healing for injuries.
data.right_text: Might help cancer cells survive treatment.

beats.caption: Researchers are still figuring it out.
beats.narration: Researchers are still working to understand how to use this without the risks. It is early days.

beats.caption: Get the full story at Headlinne.com.
beats.narration: For more science news that matters, check out Headlinne.com. Would you want your cells to work this way?
